doc.name: A — strength training catalogue, linen fold, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: urethane hex dumbbell pair
Category: strength training
Shot programme: linen fold
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the art director signing off every frame of this strength training campaign. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the top-down flat in a linen fold treatment.

SUBJECT. A urethane hex dumbbell pair. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Directly overhead, product and props arranged on a single plane. Shoot on a 40mm anamorphic at f/4, framing for a stacked layered composition with three depth planes.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with underlighting from a translucent base panel. Stage the product on or against moss and lichen, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a cinematic grade with a warm key and green-leaning ambient shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Your entire reply is the prompt itself: one dense paragraph, no title, no quotation marks, no trailing notes.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
